paragraphs: During an open day at a city fire station, visitors meet firefighters {{mask_1}} respond to emergencies across the district. A child asks {{mask_2}} a crew does when an alarm sounds. The captain introduces a fire engine {{mask_3}} carries hoses, ladders, and breathing equipment. She explains {{mask_4}} the team checks its equipment before each shift. A firefighter {{mask_5}} helmet is displayed nearby describes how protective gear is inspected.

The crew demonstrates the radio system {{mask_6}} they use to receive dispatch information. Visitors learn {{mask_7}} a dispatcher gathers details and sends the appropriate units. A volunteer asks {{mask_8}} a smoke alarm should be installed in a two-story home. The educator points to a diagram {{mask_9}} shows how smoke can travel through hallways and stairs. Families also discuss {{mask_10}} they should go to leave the building.

At the training area, a recruit {{mask_11}} joined the station last year explains how firefighters practice using ladders. The instructor asks {{mask_12}} the group would do if a doorway felt hot. She stresses that everyone should leave immediately and call emergency services from a safe place. A firefighter {{mask_13}} the visitors meet in the practice room demonstrates how a hose is handled. The team shows visitors {{mask_14}} crews use to check for hidden heat after a fire has been extinguished.

Before the event ends, the captain invites questions from the audience. One visitor wants to know {{mask_15}} firefighters decide whether a building is safe to re-enter. Another asks {{mask_16}} residents should keep in an emergency kit. The captain describes a training course {{mask_17}} prepares new recruits for demanding situations and introduces an instructor, explaining {{mask_18}} students can contact the station for more information. A local reporter, {{mask_19}} has covered several community safety events, asks how the station works with neighborhood groups. The captain thanks everyone {{mask_20}} came to learn about fire prevention and emergency response.
